keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The war of 1356: Montferrat took Asti (23 January), Alba, Mondovi and Chieri; Philip II of Taranto acquired Mondovi, Cuneo and Cherasco in June; Pavia was besieged in vain by Galeazzo in April and 'Asti and Pavia remained to the Marquis of Montferrat' in 1358. Novara 'returned to the Visconti' in 1358 and is therefore out for 1356-1357 (confidence 1). The Visconti keep the rest of Pavia province. The 1354 division among Matteo II, Bernabo and Galeazzo II is one realm for the map.

ledger.note: May 1259: Martino della Torre becomes lord of Milan. The lordship 'was created in May 1259 following the election of Martino della Torre as lord of Milan'. The land is my reading.
December 1263: Como is annexed. 'In December 1263 Filippo annexed Como to the lordship of Milan.'
1270: Lodi falls to Milan. 'Milan waged war on Lodi which fell 3 months later' (the year is the page's section heading, not in the sentence).

1271: Como revolts. 'In 1271 due to the continuous wars and the increase in taxes, countless revolts against Milanese rule followed': 'first Brescia and then Lodi, Como, Crema, Cremona and Novara'. Brescia, Crema, Cremona and Novara have no dated gain in this dossier and are not drawn before 1271 (reviewer fix of the 1259-1270 keyframe).
1271: Lodi revolts, a year after it fell (same sentence as Como).

21 January 1277: Archbishop Ottone Visconti beats the Della Torre. 'Napo della Torre was defeated and captured in the Battle of Desio on 21 January 1277 by Archbishop Ottone Visconti.' The Visconti rule begins; the state continues.

1302: the Della Torre force Matteo Visconti out. Under the Peace of Pioltello 'the Della Torre forced him to abandon the government of Milan'; the Visconti return in 1311 and definitively on 20 September 1313.

region.text: Bergamo, Alessandria (with Tortona), Vercelli and Piacenza

ledger.note: After 1313: Matteo and Galeazzo become lords of other cities. 'after the death of Henry VII in 1313, Matteo and his son Galeazzo managed to become lords of other cities in northern Italy' (Bergamo, Tortona, Alessandria, Vercelli, Piacenza). The page gives no year per city, so 1313 is a floor. Alessandria page: the Visconti appear there only in 1345 ('Alessandria went under the protection of Luchino Visconti'); the two pages are not reconciled. Montferrat's holdings (Casale from 1292, Trino) are subtracted in the keyframes.

After 1313: Como and Novara. 'Regimes favoring the Visconti settled in Como, Novara, and Pavia.' No year and no ruler: a pro-Visconti regime is not proof of Visconti rule, so this is a bridge (confidence 1).
20 September 1313: the Visconti are back for good. The city 'returned definitively into Visconti hands only on 20 September 1313 when Matteo Visconti was again appointed lord of Milan for life.'

1315: Pavia is captured. Matteo I Visconti page: after the October 1315 victory of Marco and Luchino on the Scrivia, 'which was followed by the capture of Pavia'. The province is my reading of the city's district.
1334: Cremona surrenders. 'In 1334 Cremona surrendered to Azzone.'

1337: Luchino enters Brescia. 'In 1337 Luchino entered Brescia, allowing Azzone to become Lord of the city.' The page does not name the previous holder; Mastino II della Scala 'conquered Brescia (1332)' (Mastino page).

1340: Luchino takes Asti. Asti page: 'Shortly thereafter in 1340, Luchino Visconti, Lord of Milan took control of Asti', 'an act which the rulers of the commune formally accepted in 1342'. The 15 km circle is my reading.
1346: Parma. 'In 1346 Luchino took Parma.'

ledger.counterpart: Piedmont lords (not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1347: Luchino pushes the western border. 'in 1347 he extended the western border of the Visconti dominions along a stretch of land until Mondovi and Cuneo.' Circles at the two named towns replace the earlier whole Cuneo province (reviewer fix); the page says nothing about Saluzzo or the rest of the province.

ledger.counterpart: Piedmont lords (not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1347: Alba and Chieri, as a bridge (confidence 1). The Lordship of Milan page has Montferrat conquering Alba and taking Chieri 'from the Visconti' in 1356, so both were Visconti land by then; no page opened dates their acquisition, and the 1347 western extension is the nearest dated event.
1350: Giovanni Visconti gets Bologna. 'In 1350 he obtained Bologna from the Pepoli family.'

region.text: the Ligurian lands of the Republic of Genoa

ledger.note: 1353: Genoa accepts Giovanni Visconti's lordship. 'in 1353 he accepted the lordship of Genoa'. Drawn as a vassal; the extent of Genoese territory is my reading.

October 1354: the Visconti domains are divided. 'Matteo II, Bernabo, and Galeazzo II agreed to share the power, dividing the Visconti domains according to geographic criteria'; the Lordship of Milan page has the lordship 'divided between his nephews' on 11 October 1354. One realm for the map; the shares are not otherwise on the page. [Retyped from split by the author on repair, 2026-10-31: the old split of Pavia contradicted the keyframes and the 1359 surrender of Pavia.]

region.text: the Ligurian lands of the Republic of Genoa

ledger.note: 1356: Genoa throws off the Visconti lordship. Visconti of Milan page: 'In 1356 Genoa regained its independence' (no month). The Ligurian extent is my reading, as for 1353. [Reviewer eu-13-x, 2026-10-31: the page is not silent on the end of the lordship; quote added and confidence raised from 1 to 2.]

1356: Pavia passes out of Visconti hands. The Lordship of Milan page has Galeazzo besieging Pavia in April 1356 (the siege failed; the army was beaten on 28 May) and, after the peace of 8 June 1358, 'Asti and Pavia remained to the Marquis of Montferrat'; the Visconti page has 'In 1359, Pavia surrendered to Galeazzo II'. The page does not say when the city was lost, so 1356 is a floor. Mirrors marquisate-of-montferrat.

1356: Montferrat takes Alba, Mondovi and Chieri. 'the Marquis of Montferrat also conquered Alba, Cuneo, and also took Mondovi and Chieri from the Visconti.' Cuneo goes to Philip II of Taranto (own entry). Mirrors marquisate-of-montferrat.

ledger.counterpart: league against Milan (taker not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1356: Novara leaves Visconti hands, as a bridge (confidence 1). The page says only that 'Novara and Alba returned to the Visconti' in the peace of 8 June 1358, so Novara was out of their hands by then; it does not say who held it or when it was lost.

23 January 1356: Montferrat occupies Asti. Asti page: 'John II expanded the territory of Montferrat and ultimately in 1356 took Asti from the Visconti', 'ending 16 years of control by Milan'; the Lordship of Milan page: 'The war began on 23 January 1356 with the occupation of Asti'. Mirrors marquisate-of-montferrat.

June 1356: Cuneo goes to Philip II of Taranto. Lordship of Milan page: 'The territories of Mondovi, Morozzo, Cuneo and Cherasco taken from the Visconti were acquired in June 1356' by Philip II, Prince of Taranto; the same page also has Montferrat conquering Cuneo, so the holder is a reading (confidence 2). Mondovi is booked to Montferrat above. No page has Cuneo returning to the Visconti, which ends the earlier reading of Cuneo to 1395.
8 June 1358: Alba returns to the Visconti. The peace was 'signed on 8 June 1358 in Milan in Sant'Ambrogio'; 'Novara and Alba returned to the Visconti'. Mirrors marquisate-of-montferrat.

ledger.counterpart: league against Milan (taker not named by the page)
ledger.note: 8 June 1358: Novara returns to the Visconti (same sentence as Alba).

1359: Pavia surrenders. 'In 1359, Pavia surrendered to Galeazzo II.' The page does not say the city was Montferrat's, so the counterpart is the holder named by the Lordship of Milan page for 1358. Mirrors marquisate-of-montferrat.
1370: Casale is conquered. Casale page: 'conquered by the Visconti of Milan in 1370', 'it remained under their control until 1404'. Mirrors marquisate-of-montferrat.

1379: Asti submits. Asti page: 'John ruled over Asti until 1372 but seven years later the city council submitted to Galeazzo II Visconti's authority'. 1379 is computed from the page; Galeazzo II died in 1378, so the year is not reconciled (confidence 2).

5-6 May 1385: Gian Galeazzo overthrows Bernabo. 'The death of Bernabo left Gian Galeazzo as the sole ruler of the Visconti territories'; arrest 5 May, rule from 6 May 1385 (Gian Galeazzo page); the Visconti page: 'Bernabo was deposed by his nephew in a coup'. The territory is unchanged. [Retyped from merge on repair, 2026-10-31.]

19 October 1387: Antonio della Scala flees Verona before Gian Galeazzo. 'he fled from Verona at midnight (19 October 1387), thus ending the Scaliger domination'; the Scaliger dominions had been reduced to Verona and Vicenza (Vicenza is confidence 2).

1388: Padua. 'A military campaign between 1386 and 1388 ended with the conquest of the Della Scala and' (truncated); Gian Galeazzo page: 'took Verona, Vicenza, and Padua'. The year of Padua is not on the pages; 1388 is the campaign's end.

ledger.counterpart: Louis of Valois, Duke of Orleans
ledger.note: 1389: Asti leaves the Visconti in a dowry. Asti page: Valentina Visconti married Louis of Valois, Duke of Orleans, and 'Asti would be included as part of her dowry' (the page's year is 1389).
1390: Padua reverts to the Carrara. 'He lost Padua in 1390 when it reverted to Francesco Novello da Carrara.'

wars.name: Scaliger War
wars.outcome: The league of Florence, Venice, Siena, Bologna, Perugia and, from 1337, Milan, the Este and the Gonzaga broke Mastino II della Scala, whose lands were reduced to Verona and Vicenza; Milan took Brescia in 1337.
wars.note: The war page was not opened; the dates are those of the Mastino II and Scaliger pages.

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundaries; every extent is a province-level or town-circle reading of dated acquisitions. The holdings of the Marquis of Montferrat (Casale, Trino, Asti, Pavia, Alba, Mondovi, Chieri in their years) are subtracted from every shape from 1313 on.

notes: Written from five pages and repaired 2026-10-31 after review (verdict fail) with Lordship of Milan (reopened), Visconti of Milan (reopened), Matteo I Visconti, Asti, Casale Monferrato and Alessandria. Changes: (1) the 1259-1270 keyframe now starts with Milan only and splits at 1263 (Como) and 1270 (Lodi); Brescia, Cremona and Novara are no longer drawn before 1271 because no page dates their gain (the page names them only as cities that revolted in 1271 and, for Brescia and Novara, as followers of Filippo's undated 'united front'); the 1271 loss now books Como and Lodi only. (2) The 1313 gain is split into Bergamo, Alessandria (with Tortona), Vercelli and Piacenza (the Visconti page, 'after 1313', confidence 2), Como and Novara (undated, confidence 1) and Pavia (1315, Matteo I Visconti page). (3) The whole Cuneo province is replaced by circles at Mondovi, Cuneo (1347) and Alba, Chieri (bridge); the 1356 war removes them (Cuneo to Philip II of Taranto in June 1356, no page returns it), Alba returns on 8 June 1358. (4) Pavia: out from 1356 (Montferrat; the siege of April 1356 failed), back in 1359; Asti: 1340-1356, 1379-1389; Casale 1370 on; Novara out 1356 and back 8 June 1358 (taker not named). (5) The 1354 split and 1385 merge are retyped as renames: the shares of 1354 are not on any page and contradicted the keyframes. (6) Every shape from 1313 on is drawn without the holdings that marquisate-of-montferrat now draws for the same year (Casale 1292-1370 and from 1404, Trino, Asti 1356-1372, and so on), checked cell by cell with the gazetteer so that the two dossiers do not overlap. Unsettled: the extents (no page gives an area or a boundary); when Alessandria came to the Visconti (1313 on the Visconti page, 1345 on the Alessandria page, 'protection' only); the years each other city joined after 1313; Lodi is drawn only in 1270 and is a hole in later shapes (no page opened dates its later status); the Bologna hold to 1395 (the Lordship of Milan page has Giovanni Visconti da Oleggio, podestà of Bologna, backing Montferrat in 1356, so the reading is an upper bound); the end of the Genoa lordship (1356 on the Visconti page) and its Ligurian extent; the Belluno, Feltre and Pieve di Cadore titles of Gian Galeazzo (undated); the Lordship page's 1385 reunification (it gives only 6 May 1385 as the start of Gian Galeazzo's rule); the 1395 day (5 September here, 11 May in the Duchy dossier). The commune of Milan before 1259 is a predecessor without a dossier. Gazetteer names: none.
